1.explanation:
1. lib/features/modeling/BpmnLayouter.js
   - This is the heart of BPMN sequence flow routing in bpmn-js. It computes the orthogonal waypoints whenever a connection is created or updated. The reconnection operation should trigger this layouter to recompute a fresh loop, but the current implementation fails to recognize loop cases and ends up reusing stale segments.

2. lib/features/grid-snapping/behavior/LayoutConnectionBehavior.js
   - This behavior kicks in on connection move/reconnect to snap segments to the grid and invoke the layouter for final routing. It is responsible for listening to the drag/reconnect events and calling the layouter. Because it doesn’t detect the loop scenario correctly, it ends up applying the wrong sequence of adjustments.

3. lib/draw/BpmnRenderer.js
   - Once the waypoints have been recalculated, BpmnRenderer is in charge of turning them into actual SVG paths. Any mismatch between what the layouter outputs and how the renderer interprets it will show up on screen. In loop cases, the renderer must draw the orthogonal loop correctly. We may need to adjust its path-building logic to handle the special case of reconnect loops.

Together these three modules cover: (a) detecting and recomputing the path for loops (BpmnLayouter), (b) hooking into the reconnect lifecycle to re-invoke the layouter (LayoutConnectionBehavior), and (c) turning the computed waypoints into a clean SVG shape (BpmnRenderer). Fixes in these files should restore the expected “as if drawn from scratch” loop layout.
1.bug_scenario:
When you reconnect the start or end of a BPMN sequence flow that already has more than two waypoints so that it forms a loop back onto itself, the final routed path is completely wrong. Instead of re‐laying out the connection as if the loop was drawn from scratch (with an orthogonal loop hugging the node), you end up with a ragged, mis-aligned series of segments.

The two gifs in the report show exactly that: after dragging the connection end back to the same element, the path does not snap or re-compute a clean loop but instead leaves old segments in place, producing an ugly, broken shape.

2.explanation:
• lib/modeling/BpmnLayouter.js  
  – This is the central piece that hooks into the modeling commands (reconnectStart, reconnectEnd, etc.) and recomputes the connection waypoints for BPMN flows. The bug manifests here because its layoutConnection logic doesn’t properly treat a ‘reconnect‐to‐self’ as a fresh loop and instead reuses or misplaces the existing waypoints.

• lib/features/grid-snapping/behavior/LayoutConnectionBehavior.js  
  – This behavior class participates in connection layout as part of the grid snapping feature. It further adjusts waypoints after reconnect. Its snapping/layout interplay is partly responsible for shifting the loop into the wrong shape when you finish the reconnect.

• lib/modeling/util/LineAttachmentUtil.js  
  – Provides geometry utilities for docking the start/end of a connection on a shape. Incorrect dock point calculations here will feed bad attachment points into the layouter and cause the loop’s elbows to appear in the wrong positions.
2.bug_scenario: When you take an existing sequence flow that has been manually routed through more than two waypoints, and then reconnect its start (or end) back onto its own target to form a loop, the automatic re‐layout does not reproduce the tidy loop you would get if you had drawn it from scratch. Instead the old waypoints are reused or shifted incorrectly, producing an unexpected kinked path.
